profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, traded on NASDAQ under the ticker NVDA. Its most recently reported annual revenue, from a 10-K filing covering the period ending January 25, 2026, was $215,938,000,000. The company develops hardware and software for computing, and the portion of its site captured here focuses on its AI model and inference infrastructure offerings.

NVIDIA's site describes the Nemotron family as a set of multimodal, open AI models built for agentic reasoning, covering tasks including complex reasoning, multimodal vision, retrieval-augmented generation, speech recognition, text-to-speech, neural machine translation, and document retrieval. The site states that Nemotron models are built on top of frontier open models and that NVIDIA publishes model weights, training datasets, and training techniques under the NVIDIA Open Model License, a permissive license that the company says permits use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without requiring attribution to NVIDIA. A specific variant, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, is described as designed to help agents complete specialized tasks faster, and NeMo Switchyard is described as a routing component that directs workflow steps to appropriate models. Bryan Catanzaro is identified on the site as VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA. Nemotron models are also available as NVIDIA NIM microservices, which the site describes as providing secure and scalable deployment and requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license, accessible through build.nvidia.com. Supporting tools listed on the site include NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, NIM, and compatibility with open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM.

The held facts record two tracked products: NVIDIA Nemotron, categorized as an enterprise large language model family with synthetic data generation and GPU-optimized self-hosted options, and NVIDIA NIM, categorized as cloud AI inference microservices for deploying foundation models with enterprise GPU optimization and self-hosted options. No litigation cases or MCP server registrations are recorded for the company.
